one_liner: R raster graphics devices (PNG/JPEG/TIFF/WebP) on AGG 2.4; about 1.3x faster than R's anti-aliased cairo png() on a composite ggplot2.
what_it_does: ragg implements R's graphics-device API (R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h) on top of the Anti-Grain Geometry 2.4 rasterizer, writing PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP or PPM files, an in-memory capture (agg_capture) or a recording (agg_record). agg_png(), agg_jpeg() and agg_tiff() take arguments that closely match grDevices png(), jpeg() and tiff(), and it plugs into knitr (dev = 'ragg_png'), ggsave and the RStudio/Positron graphics pane. It is not a C++ library: the device class lives behind R's graphics engine and Rinternals, so only R code can drive it.
how_it_is_fast: Every primitive goes through AGG's scanline anti-aliasing rasterizer (rasterizer_scanline_aa: exact-area coverage cells, sorted and swept per scanline) and is blended as spans straight into a premultiplied RGB/RGBA buffer by renderer_scanline_aa_solid; fills use packed scanlines (scanline_p8), strokes and dashes are turned into polygons by conv_stroke/conv_dash and rasterized the same way. Text goes through FreeType with a process-wide static agg::font_cache_manager, so repeated glyphs come from a cache; shaping is done by the textshaping package (HarfBuzz/FriBidi). Masks are applied at scanline level through masked-scanline adaptors over an alpha or luminance buffer, whereas R's cairo device pushes and pops a cairo group and calls cairo_mask for every masked primitive (cairoBegin/cairoEnd in grDevices cairoFns.c), which is why the mask and pattern tests show the largest gaps.
when_to_use: You render R plots to raster files (PNG/JPEG/TIFF/WebP) with anti-aliasing and want them faster than png(type = 'cairo'): about 245 ms vs about 320 ms for the vignette's layered ggplot2 composite.
Text-heavy plots: in the 2026-04-08 build 1000 text strings took about 19 ms with ragg vs about 81 ms with every cairo setting (about 4x, read from the plot).
Plots using grid masks or pattern fills (R >= 4.1): about 8 ms vs 37 ms for the mask test and about 94 ms vs 410 ms for the pattern test against anti-aliased cairo (read from the plots).
Headless servers, CI and knitr/pkgdown builds that need system fonts, right-to-left text, emoji and identical output across Linux, macOS and Windows without X11.
RStudio (>= 1.4) or Positron users who want the AGG backend as the interactive graphics device.
when_not_to_use: You need a 2D rasterizer callable from C++: ragg's C++ core needs R's graphics engine and Rinternals; use AGG 2.6 or Blend2D directly.

Plots that clip many primitives with a complex grid clipping path: in the 2026-04-08 build ragg took about 87 ms vs about 55 ms for cairo on the vignette's clip-path test (cairo about 1.6x faster), because ragg re-rasterizes the whole clip path for every primitive.
Many small, nearly empty images: opening and closing a device costs about 7.3 ms vs about 3 ms for png(type = 'cairo') (mostly PNG encoding and file size, per the vignette).

Fill-only output where non-anti-aliased edges are acceptable: cairo skips anti-aliasing on fills and wins on filled rectangles (about 0.85 ms vs 1.1 ms per 1000) and other single fill-heavy primitives.
Vector output (PDF, SVG): ragg is raster-only; use cairo_pdf, svglite or the pdf device.

integration.dependencies: R with the systemfonts and textshaping packages (HarfBuzz, FriBidi via textshaping); system FreeType, libpng, libtiff, libjpeg, libwebp and libwebpmux; AGG 2.4 sources are bundled and built as a static library inside the package
integration.min_toolchain: Built by R CMD INSTALL with R's configured C/C++ compiler; src/Makevars.in sets no CXX_STD, so R's default C++ standard applies (code uses C++11 features such as unique_ptr and unordered_map). pkg-config is used to find system libraries; Windows builds use Rtools.
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (Rtools, Arm Windows prepared in 1.2.6); big-endian handled through separate raster pixel formats (WORDS_BIGENDIAN)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; R graphics devices are driven from R's main thread, and the FreeType font engine and glyph cache are function-local statics shared by all ragg devices in the process
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — agg_png()/agg_jpeg()/agg_tiff() mirror the png()/jpeg()/tiff() arguments and knitr accepts dev = 'ragg_png', but there is no type or antialias argument (ragg always anti-aliases), fonts are resolved through systemfonts, and pixels will not match cairo output

gotchas: Fills are always anti-aliased, so adjacent filled shapes can show faint seams; open issue #103 (geom_tile banding on Windows) and #131 (striping between spplot polygons) report this, and 1.3.0 added rectangle snapping to the pixel grid (on by default) for fill-only rectangles.

The vignette prose is older than its plots: it calls ragg 'much better' on clipping paths and only 'slightly faster' on text, while the 2026-04-08 rendered plots show ragg slower on clipping paths and about 4x faster on text.
Loading the package can be slow when the user's local font directory is large, because systemfonts rescans it on every load (issue #210, open as of 2026-10).
Gradient stops placed very close together (e.g. 0.0001 apart) lose the flanking colours, while cairo renders them (issue #154, open).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ragg when the caller is R code and you want a faster anti-aliased replacement for png(type = 'cairo'); from C++ use the rasterizer underneath it (Anti-Grain Geometry, catalogued as AGG 2.6) or Blend2D, which beats AGG and Cairo in the catalogued third-party thesis and has a JIT pipeline that ragg does not.
verified_claims_summary: First-party bench::mark runs (min 10 iterations) in the pkgdown-rendered vignette, built 2026-04-08 on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 runner with R 4.5.3 and ragg 1.5.2 (CPU model and compiler flags not stated), timing agg_png() against png(type = 'cairo') with antialias none, gray and subpixel: the layered ggplot2 composite takes about 245 ms with ragg vs about 320-325 ms with anti-aliased cairo and about 265 ms with non-anti-aliased cairo, where a void_dev() run of the same plot (about 130 ms, single system.time call) marks the non-rendering share, so ragg's rendering part is roughly 1.6x faster (derived from page data, plot readings). R's cairo device turns anti-aliasing off for every solid fill (cairoFill sets CAIRO_ANTIALIAS_NONE), so the anti-aliased cairo settings only anti-alias strokes and text; ragg does more work on fills, not less.
status_note: Actively maintained by Posit (ragg 1.5.2 on CRAN, last commit 2026-05-13, 184 stars), MIT-licensed with AGG 2.4 under a BSD licence, and safe to adopt for R graphics; its C++ is not reusable outside R.
